sources.title: GPT-5.6 launch
sources.evidence: Dated July 9, 2026; announces general availability of the GPT-5.6 family, explicitly including Luna in API access. The naming scheme separates generation from Sol, Terra and Luna capability tiers.

sources.title: GPT-5.6 Luna API model reference
sources.evidence: Exact model ID and sole listed snapshot: gpt-5.6-luna. Documents 1,050,000 context, 922,000 maximum input and 128,000 maximum output tokens; text/image input, text output, reasoning and function calling; Responses, Chat Completions and Batch support.

sources.title: GPT-5.6 System Card
sources.evidence: The July release card identifies Luna as a GPT-5.6 family member and reports exact Luna evaluation columns. Data/training and safety sections do not disclose total or active parameter counts or network architecture.

sources.title: Public Summary of Training Content for GPT-5.6 Luna
sources.evidence: July 23 summary names Luna, states it is not a modification or fine-tune of a prior model, and records EU placement on July 9. Its numeric ranges describe training data, including audiovisual material represented partly by transcripts or metadata, not parameter counts or API capabilities.

sources.title: GPT-6 Astra System Card, including GPT-6 Sol and Luna appendix
sources.evidence: Later card and Sol/Luna appendix include GPT-5.6 Luna comparisons in HealthBench and alignment evaluations. Checked exact model mentions and training sections: evaluation scores and response lengths do not supply model size, active counts or architecture.

sources.title: GPT-6.1 Sol System Card
sources.evidence: September 29 addendum compares older models and explicitly discusses GPT-5.6 Luna in the auto-review evaluation. No production parameter count or structural architecture disclosure for GPT-5.6 Luna was found.

sources.title: GPT-6.1 Terra System Card
sources.evidence: October 26 addendum retains a specifically labeled gpt-5.6-luna HealthBench column. Its values are evaluation scores and mean response lengths; training and comparison sections do not disclose Luna parameter counts or architecture. The linked PDF was also checked.

sources.title: How GPT-5.6 fuses frontier intelligence with frontier efficiency
sources.evidence: July 29 engineering article describes KV caching and serving work across sub-networks. Architecture experiments concern a separate speculative draft model improved by Sol, not Luna. It does not specify Luna Transformer, dense or MoE structure or counts.

sources.title: The builder’s guide to GPT-5.6
sources.evidence: August 13 guide discusses Luna workload selection and training for persisted reasoning, compaction, multi-agent orchestration and programmatic tool calling. Its architectural interventions describe agent/API behavior rather than revealing Luna network topology or size.

sources.title: Prompt caching
sources.evidence: Current guide describes KV states/tensors and explicitly covers GPT-5.6 and later caching controls. KV terminology alone does not establish the complete network architecture or dense/MoE routing of this exact model.

sources.title: File inputs
sources.evidence: Vision-capable models can receive PDFs as extracted text plus page images. Responses and Chat Completions accept PDF inputs; PDF is an input format processed into the model’s text/image modalities.

sources.title: OpenAI Services Agreement
sources.evidence: Governs API service access, grants a non-exclusive right to use services, and restricts reverse engineering. Together with the exact model’s hosted distribution, supports Proprietary classification rather than an open-weight license.

sources.title: OpenAI API changelog
sources.evidence: July 9 entry explicitly releases gpt-5.6-luna alongside Sol and Terra through Responses, Chat Completions and Batch. Later July 30 pricing and August 5 fast-mode entries do not establish a new release date or parameter count.

sources.title: OpenAI API deprecations
sources.evidence: The current deprecations list mentions gpt-5.6-luna as a recommended replacement for older models; it does not list a shutdown date for this exact model. Documentation does not prove endpoint operation.

sources.title: Previewing GPT-5.6 Sol
sources.evidence: June 26 announcement includes Luna but explicitly restricts the preview to selected trusted partners and organizations. The subsequent July 9 announcement establishes general public release.

sources.title: GPT-5.6 August Updates
sources.evidence: August 6 card distinguishes the new ChatGPT Luna version from the July versions retained in Codex and Work. Training and exact July/August Luna comparisons disclose no network architecture or parameter counts.

developer.note: First-party launch and model-specific training summary identify OpenAI.

family.note: The official generation is GPT-5.6; Luna is a capability tier. Corrects the cross-generation gpt-luna grouping.

release_date.note: Explicit public/API launch date. June 26 was a restricted partner preview; August 6 concerned a later ChatGPT variant. EU placement independently agrees with July 9.

open_weights.note: Released through OpenAI-hosted services and API under service terms; the reviewed release materials do not distribute Luna checkpoints or grant weight redistribution rights.

license.note: Descriptive classification of the hosted model’s terms, not an SPDX or checkpoint license.

parameters_b.note: No total count disclosed in the reviewed exact-model training summary, original/later system cards, comparisons or engineering material. Training-data volumes, benchmark values and draft-model experiments are not Luna parameter counts.

active_parameters_b.note: No per-token active parameter count or routing breakdown disclosed. Do not infer one from the nano-tier analogy, sibling models or serving costs.

architecture.note: Exact-model and family training, engineering and later comparison sources did not establish Luna network topology. KV tensors are insufficient structural evidence; sub-networks do not establish MoE, and the separately optimized speculator is not the main model. Searches for exact-name Transformer, parameter and interpretability disclosures supplied no stronger primary evidence.

context_window.note: Documented total window; maximum input is 922,000 and output is 128,000 tokens. This is a documented limit, not an endpoint execution test.

modalities.note: Text/image inputs and text output are native API modalities. PDF is retained as a supported document format processed into text and page images. Audiovisual training data and an image-generation tool do not establish native audio/video input or image output.

reasoning.note: Explicit reasoning-token support with none, low, medium (default), high, xhigh and max efforts.

tool_call.note: Exact model documentation supports function calling and Responses tools; launch changelog also introduces programmatic tool calling.

description.value: GPT-5.6 reasoning model for high-volume workloads, accepting text and images and generating text.
description.note: Uses documented purpose and I/O; avoids unqualified speed or cost superiority claims.

patch.notes: July 9, 2026 is the public/API launch, after the June 26 restricted partner preview. The August ChatGPT update is a distinct product version. The API reference lists only the undated gpt-5.6-luna identifier as its snapshot, so no immutable date-suffixed snapshot is inferred. The documented 1,050,000-token context comprises a 922,000-token maximum input and 128,000-token maximum output. PDF denotes document input transformed into text and page images. Training-data quantities and audiovisual content in the EU summary do not establish model parameter counts or API audio/video support. Total parameters, active parameters and network architecture remain unknown; later exact-model comparisons disclose evaluation metrics, not sizes. No shutdown date for Luna appears in the reviewed deprecations list; endpoint operation was not tested.

summary: Correct family to gpt-5.6, classify license as Proprietary, replace catalog provenance with first-party evidence and use a factual description. Confirm July 9 public release, 1.05M context, text/image/PDF input, text output, reasoning and tool calling. Counts remain undisclosed and architecture unverified after original, training-summary, engineering and later exact-model comparison checks.
